GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2023-07-05T13:34:16Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: how to chose a shard for distributed 
Description: clickhouse-server version: 22.3.2

 When I use clickhouse-local to perform modulo calculation on cityHash64 pre-hashing, the results are different from using cityHash64 on ClickHouse distributed tables. I understand that ClickHouse distributed tables calculate shard modulo using cityHash64(name)%10+1, rather than CAST(cityHash64(name)%10,'Int64')+1. How can I perform the modulo calculation to achieve the same results?

example my table:
CREATE TABLE if not exists default.dist_test_babelx (
name String,
....
)
ENGINE = Distributed('{cluster}', 'default', 'test_babelx', CAST(xxHash64(name),'Int64'))

i have 10 nodes.

table data:
check sql
```
select name,  CAST(xxHash64(name),'Int64')%10,getMacro('shard') as shard from clusterAllReplicas('{cluster}',default.test_babelx) order by shard
┌─name────────┬─modulo(CAST(xxHash64(name), 'Int64'), 10)─┬─shard─┐
│ lilei6_6938 │                                        -3 │ 04    │
└─────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┘
┌─name─────────┬─modulo(CAST(xxHash64(name), 'Int64'), 10)─┬─shard─┐
│ lilei0_87531 │                                         4 │ 05    │
└──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┘
┌─name─────────┬─modulo(CAST(xxHash64(name), 'Int64'), 10)─┬─shard─┐
│ lilei9_46548 │                                        -2 │ 05    │
└──────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────┴───────┘
```

when name is “lilei9_46548“, the CAST(xxHash64('lilei9_46548'), 'Int64') equals -2574499495101583472 is a negative value.
So my question is how does the distributed table calculate the shard when the value of sharding_key is negative.
If there is no negative value, there is no problem. I understand that the calculation shard rule is abs(CAST(xxHash64(name),'Int64')%10+1).

Or to change the way of thinking, how can I use java to perform hash calculation on a certain column field, such as name, to obtain the same shard num as distributed hash calculation
